design: Adaptive instruction-development pilot, four synthetic documentation cases; full variant plus scenario/action/consequence framing prompt compared with neutral-task originals.
current_arm: All four frozen current-skill outputs are byte-identical keeps. Each shares its original observation; no duplicate independent measurement claimed.
quality_review: Separate LLM reviewer, randomized X/Y labels, no scores or arm mapping; official docs inspected, runtime behavior not reproduced.
limitations: Small synthetic convenience sample, fresh relative to prior local detector cases only.
Variant proposed after observing current-skill keep behavior; not an untouched holdout.
Baseline author had read the skill; not a context-isolated skill-naive control.
One writer output per condition, same model family, no human ratings or ordinary-editing control.
Additional framing prompt is part of the intervention; no isolated sentence effect.
Content order and length changed; quality judgments are separate from scores.
Maintainer-observed UI receipts, not authenticated service exports or independent remeasurement.
Strict verbatim receipt checker not used; effective editor text adds exactly three LF.

cases.reader_question: In PostgreSQL 17, our report runs two ordinary SELECT queries in one explicit transaction while other sessions update the tables. Can the queries see different committed data under Read Committed? Please explain how Repeatable Read changes snapshot timing, how to start it, and what to do if we later add an UPDATE and hit a concurrent-update serialization failure. Does Repeatable Read guarantee a result equivalent to serial execution?
cases.reader_context: Ordinary table queries without FOR UPDATE/SHARE, sequence operations, or application writes in the initial reporting example. Read Committed is the selected/default isolation level. The proposed later UPDATE is a separate extension of the example.
